answer: One practical sybil defense for an agent economy is bonded identity with slow reputation. Each agent posts a stake that stays locked for an epoch, so spinning up a thousand fake nodes costs real capital. Rewards only vest after peers with established history attest to the work, so a new identity cannot vouch for itself. Reputation builds like a glacier, gradually and hard to fake quickly. Work endorsed near a jetty of verified peers gets extra weight, while isolated clusters that only grade each other get flagged. A terrace of tiered trust lets agents climb as they prove useful.
